newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - RED WINGS DEAL COFFEY, PRIMEAU FOR SHANAHAN, GLYNN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - RED WINGS DEAL COFFEY, PRIMEAU FOR SHANAHAN, GLYNN.

text.p: The Detroit Red Wings on Wednesday dealt future Hall of Fame defenceman Paul Coffey and rugged forward Keith Primeau to the Hartford Whalers in exchange for former 50-goal scorer Brendan Shanahan and defenceman Brian Glynn.
The Whalers, who also received a 1997 first-round draft pick, announced the long-rumoured trade at a news conference.
The 35-year-old Coffey, a member of three of Edmonton's Stanley Cup champion teams of the 1980s, is the all-time leading scorer among defenceman.
He had 14 goals and 60 assists in 76 games for the Red Wings last season. In 1,154 career games, Coffey has 372 goals, 1,038 assists and 1,410 points -- all records for a defenceman.
Shanahan, considered one of the NHL's premier power forwards, had 44 goals and 34 assists last season for the Whalers.
The 27-year-old Shanahan, who has also played for New Jersey and St Louis, cracked the 50-goal plateau in 1993 and 1994 with the Blues. He has 289 goals and 310 assists in 634 career games.

Primeau, one of the league's most physical forwards, had been suspended by the Red Wings after failing to report to training camp following the World Cup. He had turned down a three-year, $5 million deal offered by Detroit.

Primeau had 27 goals and 25 assists and led Detroit in penalty minutes with 168 in 74 games last season, but was one of many disappointing players for the favoured Red Wings in the Stanley Cup playoffs.
The 28-year-old Glynn, a journeyman who had just four assists and no goals in 54 games for the Whalers last season, is joining his seventh NHL team.
